title: I built a tool that tells me when a live EA stops behaving like its backtest. Looking for feedback
author: br-hm
selftext:
Like a lot of people here, I'd run an EA live and then wonder whether a bad stretch was normal variance or the strategy actually breaking. A backtest tells you what drawdown to expect, but nothing tells you when live results have left that range.

So I built Watchdog. You upload your backtest report, attach a small read-only EA to the chart, and it plots your live equity against the range the backtest predicted. If the account drifts outside the band, you see it early instead of after the damage is done.

The second tool is Allocate. If you run several strategies, each one can look fine on its own while the combined drawdown blows through your limit. Allocate takes the backtest reports and sizes each strategy so the combined drawdown stays inside the limit you set.

I'd really like honest feedback. Does the "live vs backtest range" idea match how you monitor your own strategies, or do you do it differently? And what would make you not trust a tool like this?

Link in the comments if anyone wants to try it, there's a free tier and also demo data that lets you click through everything without connecting anything.
